analysis.subject: civics
analysis.pageCoverage: Page describes the timeline for electing a president of the United States, including how often elections occur and the ordered events from candidate registration and party primaries through conventions, debates, election day, electoral college voting and inauguration.

overview.headline: The presidential election cycle from registration to inauguration

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the process of electing a president takes almost two years.
keyPoints.quote: The process of electing a president takes almost two years.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that an election for president of the United States happens every four years on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November.
keyPoints.quote: An election for president of the United States happens every four years on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that states and parties hold presidential primaries and caucuses during the election cycle.
keyPoints.quote: States and parties hold presidential primaries and caucuses.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that electors cast their votes for president in the Electoral College in December before Congress counts them.
keyPoints.quote: Electors cast their votes for president in the Electoral College.

keyTerms.gloss: Contest that follows a typical cycle to choose a president
keyTerms.quote: The presidential election process follows a typical cycle:

keyTerms.gloss: Agency where candidates register to run for president
keyTerms.quote: Candidates register with the Federal Election Commission to run for president.

keyTerms.gloss: State events where parties hold contests to choose candidates
keyTerms.quote: States and parties hold presidential primaries and caucuses.

keyTerms.gloss: Meetings where parties choose their presidential candidates
keyTerms.quote: Parties hold nominating conventions to choose their presidential candidates.

keyTerms.gloss: Body where electors cast votes for president
keyTerms.quote: Electors cast their votes for president in the Electoral College.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: The page pairs time of year with event in a cycle table, so a table helps students link each phase to its place in sequence.
The page states several checkable facts about election timing and steps that students can recall directly from the wording.
componentPlan.focusQuote: An election for president of the United States happens every four years on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November.
